classification.difficultyReason: Split at the zero of the absolute-value argument, simplify each branch, and sketch two horizontal rays with excluded endpoints.

content.prompt: Simplify this expression $\frac{x-2}{|x-2|}$ and hence sketch $y=\frac{x-2}{|x-2|}$.

answer.worked:
For $x>2$, $|x-2|=x-2$:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{x-2}{|x-2|}&=\frac{x-2}{x-2}\\&=1.\end{aligned}$$
For $x<2$, $|x-2|=-(x-2)$:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{x-2}{|x-2|}&=\frac{x-2}{-(x-2)}\\&=-1.\end{aligned}$$
At $x=2$, the denominator is zero, so the expression is undefined. Sketch $y=1$ for $x>2$ and $y=-1$ for $x<2$, with open endpoints at $(2,1)$ and $(2,-1)$.

spec.description: Two blue horizontal rays with open endpoints, black arrowed coordinate axes, and dashed guides. No grid or origin label.
spec.mathematics: y=-1 for x<2 and y=1 for x>2; undefined at x=2. Open endpoints (2,-1) and (2,1).
